clue.text: I'm leader so bad there's dismay

indicators.note: bad here means badly made, so the letters of the words before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A team leader admits their poor performance has disheartened everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges IMLEADERSO, the letters of I'm leader so; 'there's' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to dishearten them, sapping their morale and confidence.

clue.text: Face being laid up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word laid is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in bed, face down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAID around in this down light; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's dial is its face, the part showing the hours.

clue.text: Shortened version of gospel is dull

indicators.note: a shortened name loses its ending, so the gospel's title is cut back

parts.note: Matthew is the first gospel of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone finds an abridged gospel tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened version of' trims MATTHEW to its familiar short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A matt finish is dull, with no gloss or shine.

clue.text: Get back, say, into wet weather

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation for say goes inside the word for wet weather

parts.note: rain is wet weather
EG (for example) means say

explanation.surface: Advice to come back indoors, for instance when it starts to rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover it, a synonym for getting it back.

clue.text: With which 'distance lends enchantment to the view'?

definitions.text: With which 'distance lends enchantment to the view'?

parts.words: With which 'distance lends enchantment to the view'
parts.note: the quotation from Thomas Campbell is read literally: a person whose eyes see faraway things clearly but near things blurred would find distant views lovelier

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Campbell's poem Pleasures of Hope, about distance making things seem beautiful; the clue reads it as an eye condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypermetropia, the eye condition where distant objects are seen better than near ones, is its everyday name.

clue.text: Extremists in society restrict organisation

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its first and last letters, here those of society

parts.note: to stem a flow is to restrict it

explanation.surface: Fringe radicals in society try to curb an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or arrangement, so organisation is a synonym.

clue.text: Old bob ate fish

parts.note: bob is slang for a shilling, a coin of pre-decimal British money, abbreviated S
had, as in had dinner, means ate

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned Bob once ate some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling (slang 'bob') was a pre-1971 British coin, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish that swims up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: No compromisers able to transform Ireland in hours

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for hours

parts.note: HRS is the standard abbreviation for hours

indicators.note: to transform the letters of Ireland is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Uncompromising figures who could change Ireland in a matter of hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to transform' rearranges Ireland to ARDLINE; 'in' sets it inside the hours abbreviation; 'able' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardliners refuse to give ground, the opposite of those willing to compromise.

clue.text: Trusty writer, expert, put in sign on proof

indicators.note: put in places the writer and expert inside the proofreading sign

parts.note: DELE is the proofreader's mark meaning delete, written on printer's proofs
a pen is a writer, the tool you write with
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A reliable author and specialist who signs off a printed proof.
explanation.walkthrough: DELE (Latin for 'delete') is the mark a proofreader writes in a margin; 'dab hand' is British for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependable can be relied upon, which is what trusty means.

clue.text: Drunk sat moaning, showing opposition

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of sat moaning are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk sitting and complaining shows hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges SATMOANING; 'showing' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is active hostility or resistance between parties, that is opposition.

clue.text: Short page, material for homework

parts.note: P is the short form, the abbreviation, of page
rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery

explanation.surface: A brief page of material set as homework.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep is British school slang for homework, short for preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, prep is work pupils do out of class hours, short for preparation.

clue.text: Schemed to get married outside the country

indicators.note: outside means the word for married wraps around the country

parts.note: mated means paired off or married
China is the country here

explanation.surface: A plot to marry abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is only a link; the definition is the past tense to match 'married'.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to plot or contrive, so machinated means plotted.

clue.text: Bishop, having got put straight, cheered up

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
righted or rightened means set upright or put straight

explanation.surface: A bishop, once corrected, felt happier.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightened describes a face or mood lifting, so cheered up is a synonym.

clue.text: Trendy type tucked into chips — terrible!

indicators.note: tucked into means the letters sit inside the words chips and terrible

explanation.surface: A fashionable person eating chips declares them awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone tucking into chips; 'tucked into' marks the letters across cHIPS TERrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster follows the latest fashions, a trendy person.

clue.text: The woman's got about a month in foreign city

indicators.note: got about means the word for the woman has got the other pieces inside it

parts.note: her means belonging to the woman
NOV is the abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: She has spent a month or so in a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is a city in northern Germany, so foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: See capital city, having organised travel in advance

parts.note: ran means organised or managed
go means travel
on means forward or in advance, as in getting on

explanation.surface: Advice to visit a capital after booking the trip ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting you to visit; Rangoon (now Yangon) was the capital of Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon was the capital of Burma until 2005, so it is a capital city.

clue.text: Excellent fighter over land and sea meets an aviator

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
RM is the Royal Marines, soldiers who fight on land and at sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: A great fighter on land and sea meets a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first class) is written AI; the Royal Marines are Britain's amphibious troops, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: An airman is a flyer, especially in an air force, so an aviator.

clue.text: Fish in earthy deposit at first

indicators.note: at first says the earthy deposit comes first, ahead of the word in

parts.note: marl is a clay-and-lime soil deposit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish found buried in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large game fish with a spear-like snout.

clue.text: Like important business (only minutes earlier?)

parts.note: a priority item sits near the top of a meeting's list, and the aside plays on items placed above the minutes of the previous meeting

explanation.walkthrough: A meeting's list usually opens with the minutes of the last meeting, so only they come higher than a top priority.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is a top priority is said to be placed near the top of the meeting's list of items.

clue.text: Group of teachers permitted to provide a bit of food

parts.note: NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British union
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A teachers' union is allowed to hand out a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT (National Union of Teachers) was a UK trade union; 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutlet is a small nut, a tiny edible kernel.

clue.text: Artist giving performance in front of her maj

indicators.note: in front of places the performance before the queen in a down light

parts.note: a turn is a performance or act on stage
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, informally Her Maj

explanation.surface: A painter performing before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her Maj' is British slang for the Queen, abbreviated ER; J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. W. Turner was a celebrated English painter of seascapes and landscapes.

clue.text: Plant grievously spreading across river and lake

indicators.note: spreading across means the word for grievously stretches around the river abbreviation

parts.note: sore, as in sore afflicted, means grievously
R is a map abbreviation for river
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A plant spreads badly over a river and lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading across' puts SORE around R to give SORRE, then L follows; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is a leafy herb with sharp-tasting leaves, a plant.

clue.text: Protester's influence, bringing in politician

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is simply the protester

indicators.note: bringing in means the word for influence takes the politician inside

parts.note: sway means influence or power
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An activist's sway over things draws in a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Swampy was the nickname of Daniel Hooper, a British eco-protester famous for tunnelling against road schemes in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Swampy was the nickname of a famous British environmental activist of the 1990s.

clue.text: In summary, become exhausted

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word before the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a brief summary; to run down is to tire or lose power, as a battery does.

clue.text: Hidden behind barrel there's a fish

indicators.note: hidden behind says the letter a sits tucked after the barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish is lurking behind a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests letters concealed in the words, but none hide it; TUN is followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, the familiar tinned kind.

clue.text: Some seen kicking around in low joint

indicators.note: around means the part taken is turned round
some means only part of the words seen kicking is taken

explanation.surface: Players spotted kicking about give a low dig in the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EENK from seEN Kicking, and 'around' turns it to read upward in this down light; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint in the lower part of the leg.

clue.text: Fateful day with teams heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for teams is removed

parts.note: sides are teams in a game

explanation.surface: A day of destiny when the teams set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops S from SIDES; 'with' is a link. The Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March, 15 March, was the day Caesar was warned of and murdered on.

clue.text: Unfortunate num — dire end — disabled

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the letters have come to grief and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy line of words about a sorry end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' rearranges NUMDIREEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Undermined means weakened or sabotaged, so disabled is a looser synonym.

clue.text: Old bird's repeating word of encouragement

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is simply the old bird

indicators.note: repeating means the word of encouragement is said twice

parts.note: do, as in 'do try', urges someone on

explanation.surface: An elderly woman keeps urging someone on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bird' looks like an elderly woman; it is the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the 1600s.

clue.text: Elders given squash containing some bits, right?

indicators.note: containing means the word for squash holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to press is to squash
a byte is a group of bits in computing, usually eight

explanation.surface: Older people are offered a squash drink with bits in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A byte is a small group of computer bits; 'squash' poses as a fruit drink with bits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Presbyters are church elders, leaders of a Presbyterian congregation.
